title: Every sharp surface is empty because the platform ledger has zero rows, and all five routes plus both pages say so explicitly rather than presenting an empty cohort as an answer
subsystem: Sharp cohort / Sharp Tracker / Sharp Roster Percentage
claimUnderTest: The audit brief asserted 'no sharp ledger database exists in this container (no .db/.sqlite anywhere, data/intel/ absent)' and asked whether an empty cohort is presented honestly or as a real answer.
observed: The brief's premise is wrong and its conclusion is right. data/intel/ledger.sqlite3 DOES exist (319 KB, fully migrated to platform-v2, with a pre-platform-v2-auto.bak beside it) but every sharp-bearing table has 0 rows: manager_seasons 0, asset_movements 0, platform_managers 0, sharp_rosters 0, sharp_roster_assets 0, transactions 0. All five routes return HTTP 200 (401 anonymously) with an explicit status string, never a fabricated number: /api/sharp/cohort and /api/sharp/market return status 'cohort_building'; /api/sharp/roster-percentage returns status 'cohort_building' with players: [], totalQualifyingPlayers: 0, cohortCoveragePct: null, lastUpdated: null and sample.rankable: false plus an 'insufficient' warning naming the 8-roster minimum. Rendered in a real browser through request interception, /market/sharp-roster-percentage shows SHARP MANAGERS 0 / ELIGIBLE ROSTERS 0 / COHORT REPRESENTED em-dash, a 'Sample too small' banner and a 'Collecting sharp rosters' empty state, with 0 console errors; /market/sharp-tracker shows 'The qualified cohort is still building' with 0 console errors. No number is invented anywhere.

reproduction.command: SECRET=$(cat /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-riskittogetthebrisket/0f0078ff-84f2-50d3-bce6-2bb1d1d8e920/scratchpad/e2e_secret.txt); curl -s -c /tmp/c.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/test/create-session -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET" >/dev/null; for r in cohort market roster-percentage; do curl -s -b /tmp/c.txt "http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/sharp/$r" | python3 -c 'import json,sys;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print(d["status"])'; done; python3 -c "import sqlite3;c=sqlite3.connect('data/intel/ledger.sqlite3');print({r[0]:c.execute('select count(*) from \"%s\"'%r[0]).fetchone()[0] for r in c.execute(\"select name from sqlite_master where type='table'\")})"
reproduction.expected: cohort_building on all three, and all sharp tables at 0 rows
reproduction.actual: cohort_building / cohort_building / cohort_building; manager_seasons 0, asset_movements 0, platform_managers 0, sharp_rosters 0

numericProof.formula: qualifiedManagers = |{m : score_percentile >= 0.75 and confidence >= 0.55}| over an empty record population

userImpact: None today: the user is told the boards are still being built and is given no number to act on.

priorFinding.note: Corrects the workstream brief's factual premise. The DB is present and migrated; it is unpopulated.

whatWorks: Three distinct empty states are separated end to end: cohort_building (no cohort), no_eligible_rosters (rosters exist but all excluded) and 'no players match these filters'. frontend/lib/sharp-roster-percentage.js::classifyEmptyState renders each differently.
rootCause: No sharp crawl has ever run in this container; the three crawl passes are systemd timers on production only.
requiredRepair: None — this is correct degradation.

title: rosterQuality is 22% of the Sharp Score and is structurally 0.0 for every manager because platform_records never populates any of its four inputs, and the weight is not renormalized
claimUnderTest: config/sharp/scoring_v2.json declares weights performance 0.36 / rosterQuality 0.22 / multiLeagueConsistency 0.22 / longevity 0.12 / activity 0.08 and says they 'must sum to 1.0 across the positive components'. src/sharp/score.py documents rosterQuality as measuring value vs league average, age-adjusted value, depth and pick capital.
observed: src/sharp/platform_records.py::build_manager_records constructs every ManagerRecord without roster_value_ratios, age_adjusted_value_ratio, depth_adjusted_value_ratio or draft_pick_capital_ratio, so all four stay at their dataclass defaults ([] and None). _roster_quality_component therefore finds `parts` empty and returns 0.0 on its `if not parts` branch for every manager, in every population. The 0.22 weight is multiplied by 0.0 and is NOT redistributed: the reachable score ceiling is 0.36+0.22+0.12+0.08 = 0.78 (plus at most +0.12 championship bonus, minus the uncertainty penalty), on a value the payload publishes as `score` on an implied 0-100 scale. Ranking order is unaffected (every manager loses the same 22 points), so qualification membership is not changed; what is wrong is the published number and the fact that a fifth of the documented model is dead code.

reproduction.expected: rosterQuality component > 0 for a manager with a strong roster
reproduction.actual: F00_rosterQuality_component_value = 0.0; roster_value_ratios = [], age/depth/pick ratios all null for every record

numericProof.formula: score = 100 * clamp(0.36*perf + 0.22*rosterQuality + 0.22*consistency + 0.12*longevity + 0.08*activity + titleBonus - penalty, 0, 1); ceiling with rosterQuality==0 is 100*(0.36+0.22+0.12+0.08) = 78.0

userImpact: A manager displayed with 'Sharp Score 68' on /market/sharp-tracker is at 68 out of a structural maximum of 78, not out of 100, and the roster-quality dimension the methodology advertises contributed nothing to their selection.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced with an exact decomposition: manual reconstruction 68.1 equals the engine's 68.1, and the 0.22 weight is verifiably multiplied by 0.0 with no renormalization.

whatWorks: The component function itself is correct and would work the moment the inputs are supplied; the percentile machinery around it is sound.
rootCause: platform_records.build_manager_records has no roster-value source. The ledger stores season results, not roster valuations.
requiredRepair: Either populate the four ratios from stored rosters (sharp_roster_assets now exists and could be joined to the board), or drop rosterQuality from the weight table and renormalize the remaining four to 1.0. Shipping a weight that is always multiplied by zero is the one option that should not survive.
dependencies: src/sharp/roster_store.py holds the roster data that would feed this.

title: score_percentile compares a ROUNDED score against an UNROUNDED population, so the top manager's percentile flips between 1.0 and (N-1)/N on a float-rounding coin flip and a two-manager pool qualifies nobody
claimUnderTest: percentile_rank's docstring: 'Midpoint handling for ties, so a population of identical values scores 0.5 rather than 1.0 - an all-identical population carries no information and must not read as universally elite.' Qualification is minScorePercentile 0.75 = top quartile of the evaluable population.
observed: score_managers stores `entry.score = round(total, 1)` (line 596) but appends the UNROUNDED `total` to `raw_scores` (line 622), then calls `percentile_rank(entry.score, raw_scores)` (line 633). A manager's own value is therefore never found in its own `equal` bucket, and whether it lands in `below` depends on which direction round() moved it in the second decimal. Measured on controlled populations with strictly distinct scores: N=2 top percentile 0.5, N=3 1.0, N=4 1.0, N=5 0.8, N=8 1.0, N=20 1.0 - a value that should monotonically approach 1 as N grows instead oscillates. The intended midpoint value is ((N-1)+0.5)/N. Concretely at N=2 the single best manager in the whole evaluable pool scores percentile 0.5, fails the 0.75 bar and does not qualify, while at N=3 the best manager scores 1.0 and does. The percentile is also published to the client as `scorePercentile`.

reproduction.expected: top-of-population percentile = ((N-1)+0.5)/N, i.e. 0.75 at N=2, 0.833 at N=3, 0.875 at N=4, 0.9 at N=5, 0.975 at N=20 - monotonic in N and never 1.0
reproduction.actual: 0.5 at N=2, 1.0 at N=3, 1.0 at N=4, 0.8 at N=5, 1.0 at N=8, 1.0 at N=20 - non-monotonic, and 1.0 for a value the docstring says must never read as 1.0

numericProof.formula: percentile_rank(r, pop) = (|{v in pop : v < r}| + 0.5*|{v in pop : v == r}|) / |pop|; with r = round(t_max,1) != t_max the self term is 0, giving (N-1)/N when round() rounds down and N/N when it rounds up, instead of the intended ((N-1)+0.5)/N

userImpact: Membership of the sharp cohort - which drives every number on both sharp boards - depends on a float rounding artifact whenever the evaluable population is small, which is exactly the state a growing cohort is in. A manager can be excluded from the cohort while being the highest-scoring manager observed.

priorFinding.note: The prior claim was that a small evaluable set can label up to half its members top-quartile. That is NOT reproduced: measured qualified shares were 0.0 (N=2), 0.333 (N=3), 0.25 (N=4), 0.4 (N=5), 0.25 (N=8), 0.3 (N=20) - never half. The real small-population defect is the rounded-vs-unrounded comparison documented here, which the prior audit did not identify.

whatWorks: percentile_rank itself is correct when given a population containing the value being ranked; the bug is entirely in the caller passing a rounded value against an unrounded population.
rootCause: Line 596 rounds for display, line 622 appends the raw value, and line 633 mixes the two.
requiredRepair: Append `entry.score` (the rounded value) to raw_scores, or rank `total` rather than `entry.score`. One line either way. Add a regression test asserting the top-of-population percentile equals ((N-1)+0.5)/N for N in 2..10.

title: multiLeagueConsistency - the anti-luck term - counts SEASON ROWS as independent leagues, and the user-facing contributor string says '6 independent leagues' for a manager with 3
claimUnderTest: score.py: 'Repeated success across INDEPENDENT leagues - the anti-luck term. Deliberately a SHARE, not a count: adding mediocre leagues cannot raise it, so "plays in many leagues" can never masquerade as skill.' config: minLeaguesForFullCredit 4.
observed: _consistency_component reads rec.finish_percentiles, which platform_records builds with ONE ENTRY PER SEASON ROW, not per league (line 152-156 iterates `seasons`, and `leagues` is computed separately as a distinct set at line 148 but never reaches this component). len(finishes) is therefore the season-row count. Measured on a synthetic manager with 6 completed seasons spread across 3 distinct dynasty leagues: finish_percentiles has 6 entries, observed_leagues is 3, and the breadth scale-down `if len(finishes) < minLeaguesForFullCredit` is bypassed because 6 >= 4 when the true league breadth is 3. The contributor string published in the payload literally reads 'Above median in 100% of 6 independent leagues'. The failure mode this is meant to prevent - one league's results reading as multi-league evidence - is reachable: a manager with two dynasty leagues and three seasons each gets 6 'independent leagues' of credit.

reproduction.expected: consistency computed over 3 independent leagues; contributor text naming 3
reproduction.actual: F03_consistency_population: elite1_finish_percentiles_n = 6, elite1_observed_leagues = 3, contributor_notes = ['Above median in 100% of 6 independent leagues']

numericProof.formula: breadth scale = min(1, len(finish_percentiles)/minLeaguesForFullCredit); correct scale = min(1, distinct_leagues/minLeaguesForFullCredit) = 3/4 = 0.75

userImpact: A manager with too few independent leagues to prove anything can receive full multi-league-consistency credit (22% of the score) and a payload string asserting a breadth they do not have.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced exactly, including the misleading user-facing contributor string.

whatWorks: The share-not-count design is right; only the population it is computed over is wrong.
rootCause: platform_records emits one finish percentile per season row and score.py treats the list length as a league count.
requiredRepair: Either aggregate finish_percentiles per league before the consistency term, or pass rec.dynasty_leagues into _consistency_component for the breadth scale and reword the contributor string to say 'season' where it means season.

title: Championship success is counted twice in the Sharp Score - once as a shrunk rate inside the performance component and again as a standalone bonus on top
claimUnderTest: config/sharp/scoring_v2.json describes the championship bonus as the implementation of 'preferably they have won the league before', 'implemented as a bounded BONUS rather than a hard gate', and separately lists championshipRate at subweight 0.26 inside performance. Neither block says the two stack.
observed: _performance_component computes a beta-binomial-shrunk championship rate, percentile-ranks it, and applies it at subweight 0.26 of the 0.36 performance weight (9.4% of the total score). _championship_bonus then ADDS up to +0.12 (12 points) to the same total for the same titles. Both fire for the same manager in the same pass. Measured: a 6-season manager with 2 championships gets championshipRate inside performance AND championshipBonus = 0.08 on top. Titles therefore carry up to ~21% of the reachable score, against a documented intent of 9.4% plus a marginal nudge.

reproduction.expected: one championship pathway
reproduction.actual: F15_championship_double_count: in_performance_subweight 0.26, separate_bonus_applied 0.08, both_nonzero true

numericProof.formula: title contribution = 0.36*0.26*percentile(shrunkRate) + min(0.12, 0.06 + 0.02*(titles-1)); at percentile 1.0 and 2 titles = 0.0936 + 0.08 = 0.1736 of a 0.78 reachable ceiling

userImpact: A lucky title carries roughly double the weight the published methodology describes, and at the margin decides cohort membership for a manager whose other evidence is ordinary.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced with both terms measured firing on the same record.

whatWorks: The shrinkage on the rate term is genuinely correct and is the right treatment for a rare event.
rootCause: The bonus was added as a product requirement ('preferably they have won the league') without removing or discounting the existing championshipRate subweight.
requiredRepair: Pick one. Either drop championshipRate from performance subWeights and renormalize, or reduce the bonus to compensate, and say in the config comment that the two are additive if they are kept.
dependencies: Interacts with W15-F002: with rosterQuality dead, the title terms are an even larger share of what actually moves.

title: The maxAbandonedRosterRate eligibility gate can never fire because abandoned_rosters is never populated, and the recency gate is vacuous for any manager not already in the cohort
claimUnderTest: config/sharp/scoring_v2.json documents seven hard eligibility gates: minCompletedSeasons, minDynastyLeagues, minLeagueAgeSeasons, minCompletedGames, minWinPct, maxAbandonedRosterRate 0.34, requireRecentActivityDays 400.
observed: maxAbandonedRosterRate: platform_records.build_manager_records never sets abandoned_rosters, so it stays at its dataclass default 0, abandoned_rate is 0.0/observed_leagues = 0.0 for every record ever built, and `rec.abandoned_rate > 0.34` is unreachable. Measured across 10 synthetic records: abandoned_rate_all_zero true, abandoned_rosters_ever_set false. requireRecentActivityDays: days_since_last_activity is derived from asset_movements rows, and scripts/crawl_sharp_activity.py crawls movements only for `qualification="automated"` members - i.e. only for managers who already qualified. A manager who has not yet qualified therefore has no movements, days_since_last_activity is None, and the gate is skipped by its own `is not None` guard. The gate can only ever be applied to managers it cannot exclude for the first time.

reproduction.expected: at least one record with a nonzero abandoned_rosters, or a documented note that the gate is inert
reproduction.actual: F09_dead_gates: abandoned_rate_all_zero true, abandoned_rosters_ever_set false over n_records 10

numericProof.formula: abandoned_rate = abandoned_rosters / observed_leagues; gate fires iff abandoned_rate > 0.34

userImpact: Two of the seven advertised quality gates are decorative; a manager who abandons rosters is not filtered out on that basis.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced. Also confirms the circularity in PRIOR-A16-F01 as the mechanism behind the recency gate half.

whatWorks: The other five gates DO fire and were each proven firing - see W15-F015.
rootCause: No abandonment signal is derived anywhere in the ledger; the field exists on the dataclass and nothing writes it.
requiredRepair: Either derive abandonment (a roster with no transactions and a bottom finish over a full season is the obvious proxy) or delete the field and the config key rather than publishing a gate that cannot fire.
dependencies: The recency half depends on breaking the crawl circularity in PRIOR-A16-F01.

title: Two ManagerRecord builders with different gates coexist; the live boards use the strict one and the operator's own scoring report uses the loose one, so they can disagree about who is qualified
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'Qualification is decided in src/sharp/score.py + config/sharp/scoring_v2.json over evidence from src/sharp/platform_records.py.' src/sharp/cohort.py: 'Do not reimplement the selection.'
observed: src/sharp/records.py::build_manager_records is a second, independent evidence builder, and scripts/crawl_sharp_records.py --score calls it. The two apply different gates for the same question. platform_records requires source_identity_type == 'global_verified', is_complete, sharp_eligible, and every one of the seven _REQUIRED_RESULT_FIELDS to be non-null, keys records by manager_key, and drops FFPC rows with no recent activity. records.py requires only `is_complete = 1 AND sharp_eligible = 1`, keys by user_id, and coerces null wins/losses/ties to 0 via `or 0`, so a season row with unknown results contributes a 0-0-0 record rather than being excluded. The operator report is therefore built from a strictly larger and dirtier population than the one the boards serve, and a manager can appear qualified in the crawl's own --score output while being invisible on both boards.

reproduction.command: grep -n 'def build_manager_records' src/sharp/records.py src/sharp/platform_records.py; grep -n 'records.build_manager_records' scripts/crawl_sharp_records.py; sed -n '365,378p' src/sharp/records.py; sed -n '44,70p' src/sharp/platform_records.py
reproduction.expected: one builder, or the operator tooling calling the same one the boards call
reproduction.actual: src/sharp/records.py:354 and src/sharp/platform_records.py:72 both define build_manager_records; scripts/crawl_sharp_records.py:77 calls records.build_manager_records() while every board calls platform_records.build_manager_records()

numericProof.formula: |gates(platform_records)| - |gates(records.py)|

userImpact: An operator running the documented `--score` pass sees a cohort that the product does not serve, and will debug the wrong population.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed including the direction: the looser builder is the one in the operator/bootstrap tooling.

whatWorks: scripts/crawl_sharp_activity.py was already migrated onto cohort_members and documents why (its docstring names the exact hazard). crawl_sharp_records.py was not.
rootCause: platform_records was added as the platform-neutral successor to records.py and the older builder was left in place with a live caller.
requiredRepair: Point scripts/crawl_sharp_records.py --score at platform_records.build_manager_records and delete records.build_manager_records, or make it a thin alias.

title: cohort_status re-derives curated FFPC membership with a WEAKER gate than cohort_members, so /api/sharp/cohort can report curated managers - and flip its status to ok - for a cohort both boards treat as empty
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'src/sharp/cohort.py::cohort_members is THE definition of who is a sharp. Every sharp-powered surface resolves its manager pool through it, and none of them may keep a second list or add a qualification rule.' src/sharp/cohort.py docstring: 'there is no second list to keep in sync.'
observed: src/sharp/service.py::cohort_status does not use cohort_members. It recomputes curated membership inline as `curated_members(config) if config.get('allowCuratedInCombinedSignals') else []`, dropping the `ffpc_enabled` conjunct that cohort.py line 221 applies (`curated_enabled = bool(ffpc_enabled and config.get('allowCuratedInCombinedSignals'))`). With enabled=false, allowCuratedInCombinedSignals=true and one verified curated entry, cohort_members returns 0 curated members and coverage.curatedManagers 0, while cohort_status reports cohort.curatedManagers 1, ffpc.curatedContributionEnabled true, and - because `status = STATUS_OK if qualifiedManagers > 0 or curated or provisional` - flips the endpoint's status from cohort_building to ok. /api/sharp/cohort and /api/sharp/market then publish different values under the identical field name cohort.curatedManagers. This is dormant with the shipped config (enabled true, allowCurated false, curatedManagers []) but it is a second membership rule living outside the single definition.

reproduction.expected: cohort_members curated count == cohort_status curated count for the same config
reproduction.actual: cohort_coverage_curatedManagers 0 and curatedContributionEnabled false, vs service_cohort_status_curated_count 1 and service_status_would_be 'ok'

numericProof.formula: cohort.py: curated = curated_members(cfg) if (enabled AND allowCurated) else []; service.py: curated = curated_members(cfg) if allowCurated else []

userImpact: With FFPC ingestion switched off for an incident, the cohort endpoint would report the tracker as healthy and name curated managers that contribute to nothing, while both boards stay empty - the exact state an operator would use this endpoint to rule out.

priorFinding.note: Not in the prior registry. The prior audit's F14 covers FFPC default-enabled config drift, which is a different claim.

whatWorks: provisional_members carries its own enabled check internally, so the provisional half of the same expression is consistent between the two call sites.
rootCause: cohort_status predates the extraction of cohort.py and was never migrated onto the coverage dict cohort_members already returns.
requiredRepair: Have cohort_status call cohort_members(qualification='all') once and read curatedManagers / provisionalManagers / curatedContributionEnabled straight off the returned coverage dict. That also removes one of the two full population rebuilds per request (W15-F014).

title: Sharp Roster Percentage publishes no per-player manager concentration, so one manager's five teams render as an 83% sharp roster percentage with nothing on the row or the page saying it is one human
claimUnderTest: docs/sharp-roster-percentage/METHODOLOGY.md: 'A sharp with five legitimate dynasty teams contributes five roster observations... Both numbers ship. transparency.eligibleRosters counts rosters; transparency.uniqueSharpManagers collapses linked accounts to humans.' Roster-weighted is stated as the product definition.
observed: Roster-weighted IS stated, and manager collapse IS published - but only at BOARD level. Every row in `players[]` carries sharpRosters, eligibleRosters, sharpRosterPct, slots, buySell, trend and sampleWarning, and NOT a unique-manager count. There is no field on the row, no query parameter and no page column from which a manager-weighted percentage can be derived. Proven on a synthetic cohort of 2 managers / 6 rosters where one manager holds 5 of them: the API returned sharpRosterPct 0.833333 with sharpRosters 5 and eligibleRosters 6 for a player rostered by exactly ONE HUMAN. The row's sampleWarning did not fire (6 >= MIN_PLAYER_DENOMINATOR 5). The board-level tiles do disclose the shape (uniqueSharpManagers 2, eligibleRosters 6, rostersPerManager 3.0), but the number a user reads and acts on is the per-row 83.3%, and nothing ties the two together. The sibling board built from the SAME cohort does not have this gap: src/sharp/market.py publishes uniqueManagers PER ASSET (canonical-manager-collapsed) and feeds manager breadth into signalStrength, i.e. the concentration hazard is guarded on one board and unguarded on the other.

reproduction.expected: a per-row unique-manager count, or a manager-weighted percentage available, for a row whose 5 holding rosters belong to 1 manager
reproduction.actual: {"assetId": "4046", "displayName": "Offense Guy", "sharpRosters": 5, "eligibleRosters": 6, "sharpRosterPct": 0.833333} with no uniqueManagers field anywhere in the row

numericProof.formula: roster-weighted = |holding rosters| / |eligible rosters| = 5/6 = 0.8333; manager-weighted = |holding managers| / |eligible managers| = 1/2 = 0.5000

userImpact: On /market/sharp-roster-percentage a user reads '83.3% of sharp rosters hold this player' as broad sharp consensus and buys or holds accordingly, when it can be one manager's portfolio conviction. The page's own footnote warns about league depth, format, cost, age and scarcity but says nothing about manager concentration, and the * small-denominator marker does not fire on this case.

priorFinding.note: The prior registry's sharp findings cover the score and the tracker; none addresses per-player roster concentration on the roster board.

whatWorks: Deduplication is genuinely structural and was proven: a roster handed the same asset twice stored exactly one row per (roster_key, canonical_asset_id) - 5 rosters x 2 duplicate assets produced 5 stored rows. GET /api/sharp/roster-percentage/audit?assetId=... DOES list managerKey for every holding roster, so the information exists behind one extra API call per player; it is simply not on the board or the page.
rootCause: The denominator design correctly focused on which rosters COULD hold a player and never revisited who OWNS those rosters at row level.
requiredRepair: Add uniqueManagers (via cohort.canonical_manager_ids over the holding rosters' manager keys) and eligibleManagers per row, exactly as market.py already does per asset; render it as a column or fold it into sampleWarning when uniqueManagers is small relative to sharpRosters. Optionally expose a manager-weighted sort. Blast radius is zero today only because the cohort is empty; it is a P1 the moment a crawl runs.
dependencies: src/sharp/cohort.py::canonical_manager_ids already exists and is already called at board level in _transparency.

title: /market/sharp-roster-percentage calls its pool 'verified sharp managers' and labels its headline tile SHARP MANAGERS, while the shipped config admits unverified provisional FFPC observers into that pool at weight 0.55 with no breakdown on the page
claimUnderTest: The page header reads 'Which players our verified sharp managers actually roster'. src/sharp/cohort.py documents provisional_members as selecting 'public FFPC observations WITHOUT claiming sharp-v2 qualification', with source rationale 'has not passed Sharp Score v2 history gates'.
observed: config/sharp/ffpc_sources.json ships enabled: true, allowProvisionalPublicInCombinedSignals: true, provisionalPublicWeight: 0.55, and ten enabled seed leagues with allowProvisionalContribution: true. cohort_members therefore admits, by default, any FFPC manager merely OBSERVED in a trade on a configured public page - zero skill evidence - into the pool that both boards read. The live payload confirms the flag is on: /api/sharp/roster-percentage returns cohort.provisionalContributionEnabled true. The tracker page handles this correctly: it shows separate AUTOMATED / CURATED / PROVISIONAL tiles, a qualification filter with four options, a qualificationLabel that changes to 'Provisional public FFPC activity', and a 'Qualification guardrail' note. The roster page renders NONE of it: buildTransparencyTiles emits managers / rosters / sleeper / ffpc / other / coverage / refresh and no qualification breakdown, there is no qualification dropdown among its seven filters so the request is always qualification=all, and the one manager count on screen is labelled 'SHARP MANAGERS'. The payload already carries cohort.automatedQualifiedManagers, curatedManagers and provisionalManagers - the page just does not read them. Blast radius today is 0 rosters because FFPC contributes no rosters at all (METHODOLOGY.md limitation 2), so this is latent until a roster-bearing FFPC URL is configured.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/sharp/roster-percentage' | python3 -m json.tool | grep -E 'provisional|automated|curated'; grep -n 'verified sharp managers' frontend/app/market/sharp-roster-percentage/page.jsx; grep -n 'qualification' frontend/app/market/sharp-roster-percentage/page.jsx
reproduction.expected: the page discloses qualification method, as its sibling does
reproduction.actual: payload has provisionalContributionEnabled true / provisionalManagers; page.jsx line 338 says 'our verified sharp managers' and contains zero occurrences of 'qualification'

numericProof.formula: count of qualification-method disclosures rendered per page

userImpact: Once FFPC rosters are ingested, a user on /market/sharp-roster-percentage reads a percentage described as coming from verified sharps that includes managers the system itself refuses to call qualified, with no way to filter them out from that page.

priorFinding.note: The prior finding says provisional managers sit in the default board under a column labelled 'Sharp managers'. That is REFUTED for /market/sharp-tracker, which discloses the three methods thoroughly and offers a qualification filter, and CONFIRMED for /market/sharp-roster-percentage, which the prior audit's scope did not include.

whatWorks: The backend never conflates the methods: CohortMember.qualification_method is carried through, _QUALIFICATION_PRIORITY resolves a manager arriving by two routes to the strongest claim, and the /api/sharp/cohort note states that curated and provisional members are never represented as sharp-v2 qualifiers.
rootCause: The roster board was built after the tracker and reused the cohort but not the tracker's disclosure surface.
requiredRepair: Add the three qualification tiles and a qualification filter to the roster page (the payload fields already exist), and change the header to 'sharp managers' or 'qualified and observed sharp managers' unless the pool really is automated-only.
dependencies: Latent until METHODOLOGY.md limitation 2 (no roster-bearing FFPC URL) is resolved.

title: Four sharp operations workflows git add a gitignored path, which exits 1 and fails the step; verify-sharp-production.yml therefore fails BEFORE the health check it exists to run
claimUnderTest: Each of these workflows ends by committing a JSON diagnostic under data/ops/ so the sharp production state is recorded in the repo.
observed: .gitignore line 45 ignores `data/`, `git ls-files data/ops/` returns 0 tracked files, and `git add` on a path matching an active ignore rule exits 1 (verified: git 2.43.0, add_exit=1). GitHub Actions runs `run:` steps under `bash -e` by default, and force-sharp-production-now.yml additionally sets `set -Eeuo pipefail` immediately above its add. So the commit step fails in all four. In force-sharp-production-now.yml, trigger-sharp-no-environment.yml and trigger-sharp-now-via-merge.yml the damage is confined to a failed final step. In verify-sharp-production.yml it is worse: the 'Commit production smoke result' step has no `|| true` and sits IMMEDIATELY BEFORE 'Enforce healthy population', which is the only step that reads sharp-production-smoke.json and raises SystemExit when status != healthy. The workflow can therefore never reach its own assertion - it fails on bookkeeping and reports red whether production is healthy or not.

reproduction.command: git ls-files data/ops/ | wc -l; git check-ignore -v data/ops/sharp-production-smoke.json; cd /tmp && rm -rf gitaddtest && mkdir gitaddtest && cd gitaddtest && git init -q . && printf 'data/\n' > .gitignore && mkdir -p data/ops && echo '{}' > data/ops/x.json && git add .gitignore && git add data/ops/x.json; echo "add_exit=$?"
reproduction.expected: 0 (git add succeeds and stages the diagnostic)
reproduction.actual: add_exit=1, with 'The following paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files: data'; and git ls-files data/ops/ == 0

numericProof.formula: exit code of `git add <ignored path>` without -f

userImpact: An operator using verify-sharp-production.yml to answer 'is the sharp cohort healthy in production' gets a red workflow that never evaluated health, and learns to ignore it.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed, and sharpened: the exit code is 1 (not merely a warning), and the ordering consequence in verify-sharp-production.yml - health enforcement placed after the failing commit - is the part that matters.

whatWorks: The smoke-check python in verify-sharp-production.yml is correct and would work if it were reached; moving the enforcement step above the commit step is a one-line fix.
rootCause: data/ was added to .gitignore; the refresh workflows that write into data/ use `git add -f`, and these four were never updated.
requiredRepair: Use `git add -f`, or drop the commit steps entirely and publish the diagnostics as workflow artifacts. Independently, move 'Enforce healthy population' ABOVE 'Commit production smoke result' so a bookkeeping failure can never mask or preempt the assertion.

title: The five 'kick sharp in prod' workflows are dead operational scaffolding: none is scheduled, four are self-triggering on their own file path, and the real cadence lives entirely in systemd timers
claimUnderTest: Six sharp workflows exist in .github/workflows/; the brief asks whether the five 'kick sharp in prod' ones are dead operational scaffolding.
observed: They are. Not one of the six has a `schedule:` trigger. check-sharp-production-now.yml is workflow_dispatch only. force-sharp-production-now.yml, trigger-sharp-no-environment.yml and trigger-sharp-now-via-merge.yml trigger on `push: branches: [main]` with `paths:` restricted to THEIR OWN yml file - i.e. they only run when somebody edits the workflow that runs them, which is a manual kick dressed as automation. verify-sharp-production.yml triggers on push to main with paths-ignore, so it fires on unrelated commits and then always fails at its git add (W15-F011). sharp-records-bootstrap.yml is workflow_run-chained plus dispatch. Three of the five names encode their own history ('force', 'now', 'no environment gate', 'via merge'). The actual recurring cadence is deploy/systemd: dynasty-sharp-discovery.timer 04:20 UTC, dynasty-sharp-records.timer, dynasty-sharp-rosters.timer, dynasty-sharp-activity.timer 06:30 UTC, dynasty-ffpc-sharp.timer 05:20 UTC - all daily, all installed by deploy/bootstrap-sharp-records.sh and deploy/install-systemd-service.sh, none referenced by any workflow.

reproduction.command: for f in .github/workflows/*sharp*.yml; do echo "== $f"; sed -n '1,12p' "$f"; done | grep -E '^(==|name:|on:|  schedule|  workflow_dispatch|  push|  workflow_run)'; ls deploy/systemd/ | grep sharp
reproduction.expected: at least one scheduled sharp workflow if GitHub Actions is the cadence
reproduction.actual: zero `schedule:` blocks across all six; five daily systemd timer templates under deploy/systemd/

numericProof.formula: count of sharp workflows with a `schedule:` key

userImpact: None directly. The cost is diagnostic: an engineer reading .github/workflows/ concludes the sharp pipeline is CI-driven and looks in the wrong place when it stops producing data.

priorFinding.note: Related to but distinct from the git-add failure: this is about the workflows' trigger design, not their final step.

whatWorks: The systemd timers are well designed and their rationale is documented in-file - dynasty-sharp-discovery.timer.template explains both the cadence and the 04:20 slot choice, and deliberately omits a [Unit] Requires= so a service failure cannot kill the schedule.
rootCause: Incident-response workflows written to force a production restart were committed and never removed.
requiredRepair: Delete the four one-shot kickers, keep verify-sharp-production.yml (fixed per W15-F011), and add a comment in .github/workflows/ pointing at deploy/systemd/ as the real cadence.

title: Waiver and free-agent movements are ingested and stored with their tx_type but no sharp route can reach them: query_movements hardcodes tx_type='trade' with no parameter, so sharp adds/drops exist as data and are Missing as a surface
claimUnderTest: The brief asks whether sharp adds/drops/trades/roster exposure are stored separately, or whether only completed-trade data exists (making the others Missing rather than empty).
observed: Storage is separate and complete: src/intel/ledger.py defines INGESTED_TX_TYPES = (trade, waiver, free_agent), stores all three with tx_type on both `transactions` and `asset_movements`, indexes idx_mv_type_ts on (tx_type, ts), and exposes TRADE_TX_TYPES / WAIVER_TX_TYPES plus a tx_types parameter on its query helpers. The in-file comment states the rule explicitly and names the historical defect it fixes ('the previous aggregator bucketed purely on add/drop and never read txType, so every waiver claim and free-agent pickup was reported to users as a buy'). But the ONLY movement reader any sharp surface uses - src/intel/platform_ledger.py::query_movements - hardcodes "m.tx_type='trade'" as an unconditional clause with no parameter to vary it, and grep shows the sole consumer of WAIVER_TX_TYPES is src/intel/service.py:616, which is the league-scoped Insider Trading product, not Sharp. So: sharp TRADES are implemented; sharp ROSTER EXPOSURE is implemented (the roster-percentage board); sharp ADDS/DROPS as a distinct signal are Missing from every sharp route and page. The buy/sell columns on the tracker are trade-side add/drop, which is correct and not the waiver signal.

reproduction.command: grep -n "tx_type='trade'" src/intel/platform_ledger.py; grep -rn 'WAIVER_TX_TYPES' --include=*.py src/ scripts/ server.py; sed -n '101,121p' src/intel/ledger.py
reproduction.expected: a tx_types parameter on query_movements, or a sharp route exposing waiver activity
reproduction.actual: platform_ledger.py:1630 `"m.tx_type='trade'",` is an unconditional clause; WAIVER_TX_TYPES has exactly one consumer, src/intel/service.py:616, in a different product

numericProof.formula: |tx types reachable through query_movements| / |tx types ingested|

userImpact: A user cannot see what the sharp cohort is claiming off waivers - arguably the higher-signal action, since a waiver claim is unilateral conviction rather than a negotiated trade. The data to answer it is already in the ledger.

priorFinding.note: Not in the prior registry.

whatWorks: Excluding waivers from BUY/SELL is correct and deliberately documented; the design decision is sound, only the read path is one-way. The board also never silently mixes them, which is the failure the comment records.
rootCause: query_movements was written for the buy/sell board and the trade filter was pushed down into the query rather than left to the caller.
requiredRepair: Add `tx_types: Sequence[str] = TRADE_TX_TYPES` to query_movements (mirroring the signature ledger.py already uses) and, if the product wants it, an explicitly labelled sharp waiver surface. Do not fold waivers into buy/sell.

title: Both imperatively registered sharp market routes ARE present in the live app, and the described fragility is real but now triple-guarded - the residual risk is a stale OpenAPI schema, not a 404
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'server.py calls _sharp_service.register_http_routes() explicitly after importing the module. The import-time side effect alone is not enough: anything that imports src.sharp.service before the app exists makes it a no-op... /api/sharp/market then 404s with no other symptom.' The shared openapi.json is annotated as the authoritative census because 'grep misses the 2 imperatively-registered sharp routes'.
observed: All five sharp paths are present in the live OpenAPI document, including both imperatively registered ones, and all five 401 anonymously and 200 authenticated. The described failure mode is real but is now guarded three ways: the module-level call at service.py:284, the explicit server.py:12743 call, and a self-heal inside cohort_status (service.py:57) that re-runs the idempotent registrar on every /api/sharp/cohort request. _server_app() also resolves the app under both 'server' and '__main__', which is the production start mode. The two roster-percentage routes were deliberately moved to plain @app.get decorators in server.py precisely because of this ordering hazard, and the docstring at server.py:12772 names the test that exposed it. Residual fragility worth recording: (1) the market handlers are registered without the response models or dependencies a decorated route would carry, and their handlers pass query params positionally into market_payload with no shared validation layer; (2) FastAPI memoizes app.openapi_schema after the first /openapi.json request, so if the cohort self-heal ever DID have to attach the routes at request time, they would work but stay invisible in the schema - a monitoring blind spot; (3) the self-heal only fires on /api/sharp/cohort, and /market/sharp-tracker fetches market and cohort concurrently, so a first market request would still 404 (the page's fetchFreshJson does list 404 as retryable, which is why this is not user-visible).

reproduction.command: python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/openapi.json'));print([p for p in sorted(d['paths']) if 'sharp' in p])"; for r in cohort market market/audit roster-percentage roster-percentage/audit; do printf '%-28s anon=' "$r"; curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} auth=' "http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/sharp/$r"; curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt "http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/sharp/$r?assetId=4046"; done
reproduction.expected: all five paths in openapi.json; 401 anon / 200 authenticated on each
reproduction.actual: ['/api/sharp/cohort','/api/sharp/market','/api/sharp/market/audit','/api/sharp/roster-percentage','/api/sharp/roster-percentage/audit']; anon 401 on all five; authenticated 200 on all five

numericProof.formula: |sharp paths in live openapi| == |sharp paths declared in code|

userImpact: None observed. The mitigation is effective.

priorFinding.note: The mechanism the prior audit flagged is confirmed present in the source, but its consequence is REFUTED at runtime: both routes are registered, in the OpenAPI schema, and serving. The prior finding predates the explicit server.py registration and the decorator migration of the roster-percentage routes.

whatWorks: Registration is idempotent (early-returns when /api/sharp/market is already in app.routes), _server_app() handles both import modes, and auth is enforced by middleware so the imperatively added routes are covered identically to decorated ones - verified by the 401s.
rootCause: Historical: routes were added from a module to avoid a second router, which coupled them to import order.
requiredRepair: Optional. Migrating the two market routes to plain @app.get in server.py, exactly as the roster-percentage pair already was, would remove the last of the ordering machinery and the self-heal.

title: cohort_members is genuinely the single membership definition, the five documented qualification gates that CAN fire were each proven firing, and an FFPC name collision cannot mint a false qualification
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: cohort_members is THE definition, no second list anywhere; qualification is documented in config/sharp/scoring_v2.json and enforced in src/sharp/score.py; platform identities are scoped per platform so an FFPC name collision cannot mint a false qualification.
observed: All three verified. (1) SINGLE DEFINITION: every membership consumer resolves through cohort_members - market.py (x3), roster_percentage.py (x2), roster_collect.py, crawl_sharp_activity.py, crawl_ffpc_sharp.py, validate_sharp_roster_percentage.py. Greps for a hardcoded roster of sharps (SHARP_MANAGERS, KNOWN_SHARPS, sharp_list) return nothing; the only configured list is curatedManagers in config/sharp/ffpc_sources.json, which is empty and gated. The one exception found is a COVERAGE recount, not a second member list - see W15-F008. (2) GATES ENFORCED, and they match the config: against a 11-manager synthetic ledger, minWinPct 0.52 rejected a 42.9% manager with the exact message 'win rate 42.9% below the 52.0% floor'; minDynastyLeagues 2 rejected a single-league manager; minCompletedSeasons 2 and minCompletedGames 24 both fired on a one-season manager; and rows with sharp_eligible=0 produced NO ManagerRecord at all. minScorePercentile 0.75 + minConfidence 0.55 then admitted 2 of 7 evaluable (28.6%), consistent with a top-quartile bar. Config and code agree on every threshold I could exercise; the two that cannot fire are W15-F006. (3) IDENTITY COLLISION: FFPC name-only identities are keyed ffpc:league:{league_id}:name:sha256(league_id\0normalized_name)[:16], so 'John Smith' in league L1 and 'John Smith' in league L2 produce DIFFERENT manager_keys (3ebe26c17572a8e9 vs f96f6a4edc691721) while 'John Smith' and 'john  smith' in the same league correctly collapse to one. And a name-only identity cannot reach automated qualification at all: platform_records._row_reasons rejects any row whose source_identity_type != global_verified with reason 'league_scoped_identity'. Injecting a 6-season, 6-championship, 12-2-per-season FFPC name-only manager - a record that would trivially clear every numeric gate - produced ffpc_name_only_automated_qualified: false with reasons ['league_scoped_identity','missing_recent_activity'].

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W15/synthetic_ledger_probe.py; grep -rn 'cohort_members' --include=*.py src/ scripts/ server.py | grep -v 'src/sharp/cohort.py'; grep -rniE 'SHARP_MANAGERS|sharp_list|KNOWN_SHARPS' --include=*.py --include=*.json src/ config/ scripts/
reproduction.expected: all consumers via cohort_members; gates firing with config-matching messages; a name-only FFPC identity denied automated qualification
reproduction.actual: cohort_members resolved at 7 non-definition call sites and no hardcoded list matched; qualification map shows each gate firing with its configured threshold in the message; ffpc_name_only_automated_qualified false

numericProof.formula: win_pct = (wins + 0.5*ties)/(wins+losses+ties) = 18/42 = 0.428571; gate fires iff win_pct < 0.52

userImpact: None - this is the positive result.

priorFinding.note: A verified negative for the 'second list' and 'FFPC collision' hypotheses the brief asked me to test. Also independently confirms the design PRIOR-A16-F14 worries about is at least enforced in code.

whatWorks: Documented above. Two further verified positives on the roster board: the per-player denominator is genuinely per position family and is never the cohort size (an IDP measured 1/1 against IDP-capable rosters while 5 offense-only rosters were correctly excluded from his denominator, and an offense player measured 5/6), and deduplication is enforced by primary key rather than caller discipline (5 rosters each handed the same asset twice stored exactly 5 rows in sharp_roster_assets). The full sharp suite passes: 194 tests, tests/sharp/, python 3.11.15.
rootCause: n/a
requiredRepair: None. Keep the identity-type gate in _row_reasons - it is the load-bearing guard against the collision path.

title: The roster board's empty state tells the user 'the sharp cohort is known' on the same screen as a SHARP MANAGERS tile reading 0, because status cohort_building is emitted for both an empty cohort and an empty roster store
claimUnderTest: frontend/lib/sharp-roster-percentage.js::classifyEmptyState is documented as distinguishing 'the three real states so "we have not collected this yet" never renders as a failure'.
observed: build_board collapses two different states onto one status: `status = 'ok' if filtered else ('cohort_building' if not stored else 'no_eligible_rosters')`. It branches on the ROSTER STORE only, never on the cohort size, so a 0-member cohort and a full cohort with no rosters both emit cohort_building. classifyEmptyState then renders 'Collecting sharp rosters - The sharp cohort is known, but its rosters have not been collected yet. Run the sharp roster crawl to populate this board.' Captured in a real browser today, that sentence sits directly beneath a tile reading SHARP MANAGERS 0 and 'Cohort represented - 0 of 0'. The instruction it gives ('run the sharp roster crawl') is also the wrong remediation: with no cohort, the roster crawl has nobody to crawl, and the correct first step is the discovery + records passes.

reproduction.expected: an empty state that distinguishes 'no cohort yet' from 'cohort exists, rosters not collected'
reproduction.actual: page renders 'SHARP MANAGERS 0 ... COHORT REPRESENTED - 0 of 0' and 'Collecting sharp rosters / The sharp cohort is known, but its rosters have not been collected yet' simultaneously

numericProof.formula: status = ok if filtered else (cohort_building if not stored else no_eligible_rosters) - has no term for len(members)

userImpact: An operator following the on-screen instruction runs the roster crawl, which does nothing, instead of the discovery and records crawls that actually need to run first.

priorFinding.note: Not in the prior registry.

whatWorks: Everything else on the empty page is honest: zeros are zeros, cohortCoveragePct is null rather than 0 or 100, lastUpdated is an em dash, the 8-roster minimum is named, and marketComparison.available is false with a paragraph explaining why no ownership feed exists. Zero console errors.
rootCause: The status enum was designed around the roster store before the cohort could independently be empty.
requiredRepair: Add a fourth status (e.g. 'no_cohort') when len(members) == 0, and give classifyEmptyState a branch naming the discovery/records crawls instead of the roster crawl.

title: Every GET on a sharp route rebuilds and re-scores the entire manager population from SQL, twice per /api/sharp/market and twice per /api/sharp/cohort, with no memoization anywhere in src/sharp
claimUnderTest: No caching claim is made, but score_managers' own docstring says population-level scoring is 'required, not a convenience' because percentile normalization is defined relative to the whole observed cohort - i.e. every request pays for the whole population.
observed: Instrumented counts of platform_records.build_manager_records (a full SELECT * FROM manager_seasons plus two GROUP BY aggregates, followed by score_managers over the whole population) per request: /api/sharp/market = 2 (market_payload calls cohort_members at line 269 and again at line 362 to build the per-platform coverage breakdown); /api/sharp/cohort = 2 (load_manager_records, then platform_records.coverage() which rebuilds); /api/sharp/roster-percentage = 1. The only lru_cache in src/sharp is on the two small JSON config loaders. The routes set Cache-Control private max-age 120-300 so a repeat browser hit is free, but every cold request and every filter change on either page (each of the roster page's seven dropdowns and the tracker's four re-fetch) pays the full cost, and the 300s auto-refresh timer on the roster page fires unconditionally. Cost is invisible today at 0 rows; it is O(season_rows) SQL + O(N log N) scoring per request at the thousands-of-managers scale discovery is designed to reach.

reproduction.expected: 1 population build per request
reproduction.actual: F12_build_manager_records_calls_per_market_request = 2, F12_calls_per_roster_percentage_request = 1, and an equivalent instrumented run of cohort_status gives 2

numericProof.formula: count of platform_records.build_manager_records invocations per HTTP request, measured by monkeypatched counter

userImpact: None at current scale. At the cohort size the discovery crawl is designed for, both sharp pages become the slowest surfaces on the site and the second build is pure waste.

priorFinding.note: The prior claim was 'two to three times per request'. Measured: exactly 2 for /api/sharp/market and 2 for /api/sharp/cohort, 1 for /api/sharp/roster-percentage. Confirmed in kind, corrected in degree.

whatWorks: roster_percentage.build_board is already down to a single build, and its buy/sell join reuses the tracker's own aggregation rather than re-querying the ledger.
rootCause: cohort_members returns (members, coverage) but market_payload needs a second, differently-filtered member list for its per-platform breakdown and calls the function again rather than partitioning the first result.
requiredRepair: In market_payload, partition the members already returned at line 269 by qualification_method and platform instead of the second cohort_members call at 362. In cohort_status, take the coverage dict from one cohort_members call (which also fixes W15-F008). Then add a short TTL memo keyed on the ledger file's (mtime_ns, size), the same fingerprint pattern src/api/bdvm_api.py already uses for the events file.

title: /api/sharp/market/audit is the only one of the five sharp routes with no Next bridge route, so it 404s in the dev topology while its three siblings proxy correctly
claimUnderTest: frontend/app/api/sharp/roster-percentage/audit/route.js's own header says it 'Mirrors /api/sharp/market/audit', implying that bridge exists.
observed: frontend/app/api/sharp/ contains cohort/, market/, roster-percentage/ and roster-percentage/audit/ - four bridges for five backend routes. GET http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/sharp/market/audit?assetId=4046 returns 404 while the same path on :8000 returns 200. In production this is invisible: deploy/nginx/chaseupside-proxy.conf routes all of /api/ to FastAPI. It matters only for dev and for any future in-app caller. Neither audit endpoint currently has a UI caller - both are API-only manual-verification surfaces, which is what CLAUDE.md describes - so nothing is broken today.

reproduction.expected: next=200 (or 401), matching the backend
reproduction.actual: next=404, backend=200

numericProof.formula: |backend sharp routes| - |next bridge routes|

userImpact: None in production. A developer following the roster-percentage/audit file's own comment to the 'mirrored' market audit bridge finds it does not exist.

priorFinding.note: Not in the prior registry.

whatWorks: The other four bridges are correct and each documents why it forwards no leagueKey (the sharp cohort is global, and scoping it would rebuild the merged feature the Insider Trading split undid).
rootCause: The market audit endpoint predates the bridge-route convention and was never backfilled.
requiredRepair: Add frontend/app/api/sharp/market/audit/route.js as a copy of the roster-percentage/audit bridge, or delete the 'Mirrors /api/sharp/market/audit' claim from that file's header.

title: completed_seasons is a league-season ROW count, so multi-league play inflates longevity and confidence while deflating the activity rate - the exact 'availability is not skill' failure the module says it prevents
claimUnderTest: src/sharp/score.py design rule 1: 'No single weak signal can qualify anyone. Being in many leagues is not skill - it is availability.' config: longevity seasonsForFullCredit 5, activity tradesPerSeasonForFullCredit 6, confidence seasonsHalfCredit 3.0.
observed: platform_records sets completed_seasons = len(seasons) where `seasons` is the list of eligible manager_season ROWS - one per (league, season) pair, not per calendar season. A manager in 3 dynasty leagues across 2 calendar years therefore reports completed_seasons = 6. Three consumers read it as a calendar-season count and all three are distorted in the same direction as league count: _longevity_component (saturating in completed_seasons) is INFLATED, compute_confidence (0.6 * seasons/(seasons+3)) is INFLATED and feeds the hard minConfidence 0.55 bar, _uncertainty_penalty is REDUCED, and _activity_component (trades / completed_seasons) is DEFLATED because trades are counted once per human while the denominator is counted per league. Measured for 3 leagues x 2 calendar seasons vs the same human's true record: longevity 0.7059 vs 0.4444 (+59%), activity 0.3333 vs 1.0 (-67%). The eligibility gate minCompletedSeasons 2 is also satisfiable by ONE calendar season played in two leagues, which is precisely the startup-draft-fallout case config/sharp/scoring_v2.json's minLeagueAgeSeasons comment exists to exclude.

reproduction.expected: longevity and activity identical for the same human regardless of how many leagues the seasons are spread over
reproduction.actual: longevity 0.7059 (6 rows) vs 0.4444 (2 calendar seasons); activity 0.3333 vs 1.0

numericProof.formula: longevity = s/(s+2.5); activity = clamp((trades/s)/6, 0, 1). With s=6: 6/8.5=0.7059 and (12/6)/6=0.3333. With the true s=2: 2/4.5=0.4444 and (12/2)/6=1.0

userImpact: A manager who plays many leagues for a short time out-scores a manager with the same results over more years on the longevity and confidence terms, and is simultaneously penalised on activity for the same reason - the score moves on league count in two directions at once.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced with a measured two-way distortion; the prior finding named the mechanism but not the opposing signs or the knock-on to compute_confidence and the minConfidence gate.

whatWorks: playoff_rate and win_pct are internally consistent (both numerator and denominator are per-row), so the performance component is not affected.
rootCause: One SQL result set serves two different questions - how many league-seasons of evidence exist, and how many calendar seasons this human has played.
requiredRepair: Add a distinct calendar-season count (COUNT(DISTINCT season)) to ManagerRecord and use it for longevity, activity and confidence, keeping the row count only where evidence volume is genuinely what is meant. Shares a root cause with W15-F004.

title: docs/intel/FFPC_UNIFIED_SHARP.md says FFPC is 'public-only, read-only, and disabled by default' and prints a config with enabled false; the shipped config enables FFPC and turns provisional contribution on
claimUnderTest: docs/intel/FFPC_UNIFIED_SHARP.md line 93: 'The first implementation is deliberately public-only, read-only, and disabled by default.' Line 121 shows the config with "enabled": false.
observed: config/sharp/ffpc_sources.json ships enabled: true, allowProvisionalPublicInCombinedSignals: true, provisionalPublicWeight: 0.55 and ten enabled seed leagues. The live /api/sharp/cohort payload confirms it: ffpc.enabled true, ffpc.provisionalContributionEnabled true. Only allowCuratedInCombinedSignals is false. So the safety posture the document describes is not the posture that ships, and a reader auditing the default has to open the config to find out. (authenticatedApi.enabled IS false as documented, which is the part that matters most for credentials.)

reproduction.command: sed -n '93p;121p' docs/intel/FFPC_UNIFIED_SHARP.md; python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('config/sharp/ffpc_sources.json'));print({k:d[k] for k in ('enabled','allowCuratedInCombinedSignals','allowProvisionalPublicInCombinedSignals','provisionalPublicWeight')})"; curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/sharp/cohort | python3 -c 'import json,sys;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["ffpc"])'
reproduction.expected: enabled false, matching the document
reproduction.actual: {'enabled': True, 'allowCuratedInCombinedSignals': False, 'allowProvisionalPublicInCombinedSignals': True, 'provisionalPublicWeight': 0.55}; live payload {'enabled': True, 'mode': 'public_only', 'curatedContributionEnabled': False, 'provisionalContributionEnabled': True}

numericProof.formula: documented default == shipped default

userImpact: An operator trusting the document believes no FFPC data can enter the cohort without an explicit opt-in. Compounds W15-F010, where the roster page does not disclose provisional membership at all.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced against both the shipped config and the live payload.

whatWorks: authenticatedApi.enabled is false as documented, and cohort.py never lets an FFPC member be reported as a sharp-v2 qualifier regardless of the flags.
rootCause: The document was written for the initial rollout and the config was flipped on afterwards.
requiredRepair: Update the document to state the shipped default and the provisional weight, or turn the flags back off. Do not leave the two disagreeing about a data-inclusion default.

title: The championship-bonus table in docs/intel/SHARP_SCORE.md is wrong for four or more titles: it says 3+ scores +0.10 while the code returns the 0.12 cap from four titles up
claimUnderTest: docs/intel/SHARP_SCORE.md publishes a title-count to bonus table ending '| 3+ | +0.10, capped at 0.12 |'.
observed: _championship_bonus computes min(maxBonus, bonusFirstTitle + bonusPerAdditionalTitle * (titles - 1)) = min(0.12, 0.06 + 0.02*(t-1)). t=1 -> 0.06, t=2 -> 0.08, t=3 -> 0.10, t=4 -> 0.12, t>=5 -> 0.12.
